common.notAllowed: Your role does not include this page.

privilege.pii_processor: PII processor — sees personal data unmasked
privilege.category: data category — may read its objects

login.title: Sign in
login.intro: Sign in with your company account.
login.asLocal: Signing in as the local administrator, gaia-admin.
login.failed: Sign-in failed. Check your user name and password; if they are right, your account may have no Gaia role yet — ask your administrator.
login.unavailable: Gaia cannot be reached right now.
login.nothing: No way to sign in is set up yet. An administrator sets the local account's password on the server (make admin-user).
login.haveCode: I have a setup code for the local administrator

setup.title: Set up the local administrator
setup.intro: Enter the one-time code printed by `make admin-user ARGS=setup-code` on the server, and choose the password of gaia-admin (at least 12 characters).
setup.done: The password is set. Sign in as the local administrator.

home.title: Welcome, {{name}}

role.user: You ask questions about the data your role covers: open “Chat”.
role.sme: You review what Gaia understood about the data sources assigned to you: open “Review”.
role.admin: You connect data sources and the company directory, define the data categories, and decide who may read what. You chat within the categories granted to you.
role.auditor: You audit the administrators' decisions: who may see what, who is a PII processor, every grant and sign-in.

home.smeSources: You are the SME of {{count}} data source(s).
home.pii: You are a PII processor: personal data is shown to you unmasked.
home.local: You are signed in with the local administrator account, which is meant for setup and emergencies. Its every use is shown to the auditor.
home.next: Everyone who chats gets answers only from the data categories granted to them.
home.noCategories: No data category is granted to you yet, so the chat has nothing to answer from. Ask your administrator.

dataSources.title: Data sources
dataSources.intro: The databases Gaia may read. A new one stays unusable until its read-only probe passes; passwords are encrypted and never shown.
dataSources.name: Name
dataSources.addIntro: Use a login that can only read. Gaia proves it before using it (nine checks, the same as make check-target).
dataSources.confirmRemove: Remove {{name}}? Its history is kept; its password is deleted.

directories.title: Company directories
directories.intro: People sign in with their directory account; Gaia reads their roles from it. The connection always uses TLS; the service account's password is encrypted and never shown.
directories.syncResult: Last read: {{users}} user(s), {{roles}} role(s); {{gone}} role(s) gone, {{disabled}} account(s) disabled since.
directories.confirmDisable: Disable {{name}}? Everyone signed in through it is signed out.
directories.addIntro: Active Directory or another LDAP server, or Microsoft Entra ID.
directories.name: Name
directories.tlsVerify: Verify the server certificate (leave on outside tests)
directories.caFile: CA certificate file on the server (optional)
directories.userBase: Where people are (optional: the base DN)
directories.rolesIntro: How Gaia reads someone's roles from the directory. You then grant Gaia roles to these directory roles, or to single people.
directories.entraIntro: Register an app in Entra ID (App registrations): a Web redirect URI — the callback below — a client secret, and the Microsoft Graph application permissions User.Read.All and GroupMember.Read.All with admin consent. People then sign in at Microsoft; Gaia never sees their password.
directories.redirectUri: Redirect URI (as registered; empty: this site's)
directories.userFilterOdata: Which users to read (optional OData filter)
directories.namePrefix: Only groups whose name starts with

grants.title: Roles & grants
grants.intro: You decide who may do what. Grants are never deleted: a revocation is dated and signed, and every change goes to the auditor. An administrator cannot also be an SME or an auditor — such grants are kept but not applied. Data categories decide what someone may read: nothing is readable until a category is granted.
grants.noRoles: No roles read yet: run “Read users and roles” on the directory.
grants.subject: Given to
grants.revokeWhy: Revoke “{{privilege}}” of {{subject}}? A note for the auditor (optional):

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.intro: Everyone who signed in or was read from a directory, their directory roles, and what Gaia lets them do now.

audit.intro: Read-only: the administrators' decisions and every sign-in, from an append-only, hash-chained log.
audit.chainBroken: The audit log has been altered
audit.head: Head hash
audit.headWhy: Write this down outside Gaia (a ticket, an e-mail). Later, it proves that nothing before it was rewritten — even by someone with full database access.
audit.accessIntro: Every account with the roles in force and where they come from.
audit.piiIntro: Everyone who sees personal data unmasked, and through which grant.
audit.subject: Subject
audit.categoriesTitle: Data categories: what is in them, who may read them
audit.categoriesIntro: Each category with its objects (proposed by Gaia or confirmed by an SME or administrator) and everyone who may read it, with the grant it comes through.
audit.refusalsIntro: Questions whose query reached for data outside the asker's categories, or used personal data they may only see masked. The asker was told only that their role does not cover it; here is what it reached for.

refusalCodes.personal_data: personal data used, not only shown

review.title: Review
review.intro: What Gaia understood about your data sources, and what it is unsure of. Your decisions are signed with your name, kept when Gaia re-reads the database, and used at once by the question answering.
review.noSources: You are not the SME of any data source. An administrator assigns data sources to SMEs.
review.staleCount: {{count}} decision(s) to look at again: the column changed since

tabHelp.open: Most important first: where a wrong meaning would cost most and Gaia is least sure.
tabHelp.done: Items decided already, the latest first. Open one to change the decision.
tabHelp.stale: Decisions whose column changed in the database since. They are no longer used; look at them again.

empty.open: Nothing is waiting. Gaia is sure enough of everything else, or it has been decided.

reasonHelp.abstain: The certainty is too low to use the meaning as a fact.
reasonHelp.evidence_exhausted: Profiling and tests are done; only a person can settle it.
reasonHelp.contradiction: Some evidence says otherwise — see Evidence.
reasonHelp.critique_disagrees: A second model reading found the meaning doubtful.
reasonHelp.test_not_run: A test of Gaia's claim could not run (time or budget).
reasonHelp.input_reviewed: A column this view column is computed from was reviewed: check whether the computation changes its meaning.
reasonHelp.stale_decision: An SME decided this column, and it changed in the database since.

summary.none: Gaia has no meaning for this column yet (run make reason).
summary.score: Certainty {{score}} ({{band}}), from {{supports}} piece(s) of evidence for and {{contradicts}} against.
summary.tests: {{passed}} of {{total}} test(s) of Gaia's claims passed.

actionHelp.accept: Gaia's meaning is right as it stands.
actionHelp.correct: Right once edited — including what each code means.
actionHelp.reject: Wrong; say why. Gaia stops using it.
actionHelp.unused: Nobody uses this column (legacy, empty). It leaves the question answering.

review.correctIntro: Change what is wrong; what you leave is kept.
review.meaningsHelp: For a code: what each value stands for (2 = overdue). The SQL generator sees these. The most frequent values are listed; add others.
review.propagated: The views that show this column took the decision: {{views}}.
review.propagateLater: A reasoning run is busy; the views {{views}} take the decision with the next run.
review.requeued: Computed from this column, queued for a look: {{columns}}.
review.inherited: This view column shows {{base}} as it is. Review that column; the decision comes here by itself.
review.noMeaning: Gaia has no meaning here yet: it has not reasoned about this table (make reason).
review.masked: Personal data: values are shown as their shape only (a = letter, 9 = digit). PII processors see them.
review.questionsHelp: Approximate: questions whose query read this table and mentioned the column.
review.tablesIntro: Every table and view, whether or not something of it waits for you. Open one to see its columns and to review any of them.
review.noCategories: No data categories are defined yet (an administrator defines them).
review.categoryIntro: The category decides who may read this object; which roles hold it is the administrator's decision.
review.categoryProposed: {{name}} — proposed by Gaia ({{why}}). Confirm it, or choose another.
review.categoryNone: No category: nobody can read this object in the chat.

glossary.title: Glossary — {{ds}}
glossary.intro: Business terms and what they mean in this data source. When a question uses a term (or one of its other names), the SQL generator gets its definition. Say it in terms of the data: “an invoice whose status is 2”.
glossary.confirmWithdraw: Withdraw “{{term}}”? It is kept in the history and no longer used.

categories.title: Data categories
categories.intro: Need-to-know: every object of a data source belongs to one category (Sales, Finance, HR …); a person may read an object only if a category grant covers it — nothing is readable until granted. Gaia proposes each object's category, an SME confirms what the data is, you decide who may read it (Roles & grants). Personal data is shown unmasked only to PII processors.
categories.none: No category yet. Create them from the schemas of a data source below, or add them one by one.
categories.name: Name
categories.keywordsPrompt: Keywords of {{name}} (comma-separated) — Gaia matches them against schema and object names and meanings:
categories.confirmRetire: Retire {{name}}? Only possible when no object is in it; its grants stay on record.
categories.objectsIntro: Set a category here, or let Gaia propose them; an SME confirms on the review screen. An object without a category is readable by nobody.
categories.proposeDone: Gaia proposed {{proposed}}; {{kept}} confirmed kept; {{none}} without a proposal (no match, or a tie).
categories.missing: {{count}} object(s) have no category: nobody can read them.

chat.title: Chat
chat.nothingToRead: Your role covers no data yet, so there is nothing to ask about. Ask your administrator for a data category.
chat.intro: Ask a question about {{ds}} in your own words. Gaia answers from the data your role covers, shows the table first, then explains it.
chat.question: Your question
chat.placeholder: e.g. Which three store cities sold the most last month?
chat.answerPlaceholder: Choose an option above, or answer in your own words
chat.clarifyHint: Choose one, or type your own answer below.
chat.maskedLive: Personal data is masked for you (it needs the PII-processor permission).
chat.maskedStored: Personal data is not kept in the conversation: it is masked here.
chat.rowsKept: Kept with the conversation: {{kept}} of {{total}} rows. Ask again for all of them.
chat.capped: The result stops at the row limit; there may be more.
chat.uncertain: Meanings not yet confirmed by an expert

queries.title: Queries
queries.intro: The SQL behind the answers, with what the guard decided and what ran. SMEs see the queries of the data sources they review; administrators and auditors all of them. People who only chat never see SQL.
queries.question: Question
queries.reachedFor: Refused by need-to-know; it reached for: {{what}}

runs.title: Runs
runs.intro: What Gaia ran to understand the data sources, and what the model calls cost (read-only; starting and scheduling runs come later).
